The Police Sub-Inspector of Jayanagara Police Station, Bengaluru has filed Police Report against accused No.1 to 5 alleging that they have committed the offences punishable under Sections 384 and 420 of the Indian Penal Code.
2. It is the case of the Prosecution that the informant is the owner of the company by name Future Capital Holding Limited.
The informant is providing loan to the customers on gold.
On 10.03.2012 one Mr.Sanjeev came to their office and told that they have already pledged the gold of 531 grams at Mahaveer Co-Operative Society by taking an amount of Rs.8,45,000/-.
They have requested to give loan to release the said gold.
The informant initially neglected the offer of Mr.Sanjeev Kumar.
But however on 16.03.2012 at about 10.15 a.m. Mr.Sanjeev Kumar again called him for the gold loan.
He has produced the Voter Card and Receipt to show that they have pledged the said gold at Mahaveer Co- Operative Society.
This Mr.Sanjeev Kumar asked the informant to come along with cash of Rs.8,85,000/- in his car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-MS-4253 to release the said gold pledged at Mahaveer Co-Operative Society.
The informant believing the words of Sanjeev Kumar went in the car sent by Sanjeev Kumar.
When the car was at J.P.Nagar, two unknown persons were came and restrained the said car.
They got inside the car and put the driver on dire consequences.
They have taken the said car towards the C.K.Palya and extorted all the money of Rs.8,85,000/-.
They forced the informant to get out of the car and went away.
Soon after the incident, the informant had been to the Police Station and lodged the information against the accused persons.
3. Based on the First Information of CW1, the crime was registered in Crime No.137/2012 at Jayanagara Police Station.
Accused No.1 was arrested and produced before this Court and released on bail.
Accused No.2 and 4 are left out from the charge sheet.

The presence of accused No.3 and 5 could not be secured, hence as per order dated 28.11.2022 the case against them was ordered for Split Up and Criminal Case No.37457/2022 was registered against them.

On completion of the investigation, the Police Sub-Inspector of Jayanagara Police Station, Bengaluru City filed Police Report against accused No.1 alleging that he has committed the offences punishable under Sections Mahesh H.S vs Chandrshekar Alias Chandru on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112687849/

sentences.text: After taking cognizance of the said offences, the process was issued to accused No.1.
The copies of the Police Report and other prosecution papers are furnished to accused No.1 under Section 207 of Cr.P.C.

After hearing, since there were grounds for presuming that accused No.1 has committed the offences triable by this Court, charges for the offences has been framed and read over to him in Kannada language.
He has pleaded not guilty and claims to be tried.
4. To prove the charges framed against accused No.1, the Prosecution has produced oral evidence of PW1 and no documentary evidences are got marked.

After completion of the prosecution evidences,
for the purpose of enabling accused No.1 personally to explain any circumstances appearing in the evidences of the Prosecution against him, examined accused No.1 under Section 313 of Cr.P.C.
He has submitted that he has no defense evidence.
5. Heard the arguments of learned Senior Assistant Public Prosecutor and the learned counsel for accused No.1.
Perused the materials available on record.

6. The points for determination are;
1. Whether prosecution has proved beyond all reasonable doubts that accused No.1 has committed the offences punishable under Sections 384 and 420 of the Indian Penal Code ?
2. What order or sentence?
7.

Point No.1 : In the Negative,

9. To prove the guilt of the accused, the Prosecution has examined CW12/PW1 Venkatesh V., Head Constable, wherein this witness has deposed that CW13 an Investigation Officer has direction CW7 to CW11 along with him to secure the accused.
These accused were secured as per their information and produced before CW13.
The Investigation Officer has recorded his statement.
10. On perusal, the information was lodged on 16.03.2012 on the ground that these accused have extorted an amount of Rs.8,85,000/- from the informant.
The information was lodged against some unknown person.
CW13 being an Investigation Officer directed CW7 to CW12 to secure the accused.
CW12 during the course of patrolling and on information had been to Marenahalli and caught hold all the four accused and produced before CW13.
Immediately, CW13 had been to the place of incident and in the presence of CW2 and CW3 has conducted panchanama.

Further, the Investigation Officer has recorded the statement of the witnesses and after due investigation CW13 Mahesh H.S vs Chandrshekar Alias Chandru on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112687849/

sentences.text: To prove the guilt of the accused, the Prosecution has relied only the evidence of CW12 but, the Prosecution even has not secured CW1 who has lodged the information against this accused.
The information was lodged against the accused on 16.03.2012 and since then accused No.1 is regular to the Court for the offences punishable under Sections 384 and 420 of the Indian Penal Code.
My Predecessor has issued summons, warrant and proclamation to secure the witnesses.

But,
in spite of even proclamation, the prosecution failed to secure the witnesses.
The Prosecution even unable to examine the informant before this Court to prove the guilt of accused No.1.
My Predecessor has dropped all the Prosecution witnesses after giving sufficient opportunity to secure the witnesses.
The matter is pending since 2012 and in spite of passing of 15 years, the evidence available before this Court is the only evidence of CW12 who is a Head Constable.
But, to corroborate the evidence of CW12, there is no evidence available before this Court to prove the guilt of accused No.1 beyond all reasonable doubt.
Hence, I answer Point No.1 in the Negative.
11. POINT No.2 :- For the reasons stated in Point No.1, the prosecution has not proved the guilt of accused No.1 for the said offences beyond all reasonable doubts.
Therefore, accused No.1 is not found guilty for the offences punishable under Sections 384 and 420 of the Indian Penal Code .

In the result, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDERS Under Section 248(1) of Cr.P.C, accused No.1 is hereby acquitted for the offences punishable under Sections 384 and 420 of the Indian Penal Code.
His bail bonds and surety bond will be canceled after the appeal period.
